_readme: THE APPLY ORDER OF supabase/migrations/**. This is the single source of truth
for rebuilding the database from the repo, and it is verified on every push by
tests/schema-drift.mjs (via tests/schema-replay.mjs).
WHY THIS FILE HAS TO EXIST. Filename order does NOT replay. Measured
2026-08-14: applying supabase/schema.sql + every migration in filename order
gets 23 of 41 files in and fails the other 18. Two reasons, both structural:
1. '2026-08-08-clan-seat-2.sql' sorts BEFORE '2026-08-08-clan-seat.sql',
because '-' (0x2D) < '.' (0x2E). The -2 file's first act is to check that
clan_board exists and raise if it does not, so it fails first, every time.
2. Nine files are dated 2026-08-11 and alphabetical order puts 'accrual',
'accrue-gate', 'anon-execute-lockdown', 'apply-engine' and
'authenticated-surface-lockdown' all BEFORE 'player-state' — which is the
foundation every one of them depends on. There is no naming scheme that
rescues this after the fact.
Before this file, the working order existed only as a hand-maintained const
array inside tests/pglite-chain.mjs and another inside
tests/conservation-fuzz.mjs, each covering a DIFFERENT SUBSET of the
migrations, and neither one covering all of them. That means the order
required to rebuild the database was not written down anywhere.
RULES:
· Every .sql file in supabase/migrations/ must appear exactly once, across
'pre_schema', 'order' and 'excluded'. The guard FAILS on a file that is in
none of them — so a new migration cannot be silently left out of the
rebuild. The full apply sequence is: pre_schema, then supabase/schema.sql,
then order.
· A new migration goes where it actually has to run, not where its date
puts it.
· 'excluded' is a claim that a rebuilt database is CORRECT without the file.
Never add one to make the chain go green.

_why: GUCs production was actually applied with, not shortcuts.
it, and production was applied with it set on 2026-08-13 (that is what closed
A11). A rebuild that omitted it would leave beta_invites world-readable and
the file would tell you so, loudly.
market_wipe_ok: read by 2026-08-17-market-v2.sql, which is in 'order'
(staged; it supersedes and deletes the old 2026-08-11-market-v2.sql). The
GUC gates that file's DROP...CASCADE of the live market tables.

_pre_schema_why: supabase/schema.sql creates game_saves and game_events with `create table if
not exists` as a bootstrap fallback, and its own header says they are assumed
to already exist. Those fallback definitions do not match production: different
primary key on game_saves, different COLUMN NAMES on game_events (kind vs
event_type, created_at vs occurred_at). Running the true shapes first makes
schema.sql's fallback no-op on a rebuild exactly as it no-ops on production.
The alternative — ALTER + rename the columns afterwards — is a rename on the
table holding every player's save, which cannot be rolled forward past a
failure. Ordering is reversible; that is not.

_order_notes.2026-08-18-enchant.sql: ELEMENTS/ENCHANTING v1, the server half. It TAKES OVER from 2026-08-18-skill-row-upsert.sql as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_apply, AND from 2026-08-17-fight-carry.sql as the last that may replace hr_state_of, so it must sit after BOTH. Both bodies are GENERATED by tools/derive-enchant.mjs from those two files and patched at named anchors (hr_apply six, hr_state_of one); `node tools/derive-enchant.mjs --check` runs in the suite, so neither can be hand-edited. Applied BEFORE skill-row-upsert it would be silently deleted by it (taking the enchant delta key + block with it while the player_state.enchant column survived — the enchant intent would then propose an `enchant` key at an hr_apply that refuses unknown keys, and every enchant would 409); its §0 REFUSES that case by requiring skill-row-upsert's `on conflict (user_id, slot, skill_id)` and fight-carry's `'fight', v_st.fight` to already be in the live bodies. What it ships: player_state.enchant (jsonb, NULL default read as {}), hr_state_of returns `enchant` top-level, and hr_apply gains the `enchant` delta key + a TRANSFER block (resolve rune->element via hr_runes, weapon-holds-weapon gate, debit the rune = ownership check, set the enchant state) + the §S5 accrued_to stamp on `enchant` (so the enchant intent's collect-before-enchant order is enforced, closing the 'fight cheap all night, enchant, settle' class) + `enchant` on c_ledger_kinds (journal.kind:'enchant') + `bad_enchant` on c_release_codes (shape refusal, like bad_equip; insufficient_item stays OFF — the ownership check must not release its key or a dupe gets a free retry loop). Real predecessors: everything skill-row-upsert names, plus 2026-08-11-catalogue.generated.sql for hr_runes (§0 REFUSES to install without the table; regenerate it with `node tools/gen-catalogues.mjs` after the rune `element` data lands in src/data/items.js) and hr_items.kind='weapon' (the weapon gate). ⚠ hr_runes IS SEEDED FROM src/data/items.js tag:'rune' items — a rune added there is a deploy-order dependency exactly like a monster hp (regenerate + apply the catalogue BEFORE the Edge payload). SAFE with a staged deploy: an old payload never sends an enchant delta; a new payload against an unpatched database gets unknown_delta_key. Graded by tests/enchant-intent.mjs.
_order_notes.2026-08-18-leaderboard-server-source.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (Security review REQUIRED — it MOVES AUTHORITY: every leaderboard score). Security condition S2. LAST OF ALL, and it TAKES OVER from 2026-08-08-leaderboards.sql as the last file that may define public.leaderboard_ranked and the last that may `create or replace` public.hr_leaderboard(text,int,int). It touches NO body any derivation chain grades — not hr_apply, not hr_rate_gate, not hr_perks_of, not hr_assert_grant_hygiene. What it ships: leaderboard_ranked is rebuilt over player_state (gold, updated_at) and player_skills (xp, with levels derived through hr_level_from_xp) instead of over game_saves.snapshot, which is the CLIENT-AUTHORED save blob — so `G.gold = 1e12` -> autosave no longer buys the #1 Wealth slot, nor any skill/total/combat rank. It also drops the `gs.snapshot->>'playerName'` fallback in the name column, which let a player with no profiles row publish a display name of their own choosing to every other player's screen. ⚠ TWO BOARDS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT REBUILT AND ARE DECLARED UNSOURCED via public.hr_lb_unsourced(): `renown` (computeRenown reads quests, the collection log, the streak and the bestiary — none server-owned; 2026-08-15-perk-channel.sql:261 already records 'blocked:no_server_renown_score') and `bosses` (summed from G.bestiary against the client MONSTERS table; hr_hunt_bosses is the CLAN raid boss, a different quantity). They keep their board ids so hr_leaderboard answers with an EMPTY, FLAGGED board rather than `unknown_board` — the client still offers those chips and an error screen would be a worse failure than an empty roll — and the response gains ADDITIVE keys `available` + `unavailable`, which src/features/leaderboards.js reduceBoard() ignores, so the client needs no change to keep working. Hiding those two chips is the follow-up client half. ⚠ THE REVOKE IN §2 IS LOAD-BEARING: 2026-08-14-leaderboard-view-lockdown.sql revoked client SELECT on the matview (F5), but that ACL belonged to the object THIS FILE DROPS, and the replacement inherits Supabase's schema default privileges (`grant all on tables to anon, authenticated`) — so doing nothing would silently reopen a `/rest/v1/leaderboard_ranked?limit=100000` dump of every player's uuid and name. §6(b) asserts the revoke took, for both roles. §0's predecessor gate is BEHAVIOURAL and DISCRIMINATING per the SKILL-8 lesson: it requires hr_lb_skills() to contain 'stonemason', a term ABSENT from 2026-08-08-leaderboards.sql's fifteen-entry body and PRESENT in 2026-08-17-leaderboard-skills.sql's seventeen — anchoring on anything both files mention would let it install onto a database that never received the skills migration and silently drop two boards from a view that had just been rebuilt. §6(a) reads pg_depend for the load-bearing claim (no dependency on game_saves) WITH a positive control (it must depend on player_state), because a one-sided dependency probe rubber-stamps exactly this kind of assertion. Real predecessors: 2026-08-08-leaderboards.sql (the matview, leaderboard_meta, hr_leaderboard_refresh, hr_lb_boards), 2026-08-17-leaderboard-skills.sql (the seventeen-skill namespace, gated in §0), 2026-08-11-player-state.sql (player_state, player_skills, hr_xp_table, hr_level_from_xp, hr_total_level — §6(g) cross-checks the view's total_level against that function, two independent expressions of one fact), 2026-08-14-character-bootstrap.sql (the seeded skill rows a fresh character ranks on), 2026-08-14-leaderboard-view-lockdown.sql (the F5 revoke §2 must re-establish). ⚠ `saved_at` IN A RANKED ROW IS NULL ON PURPOSE, AND IT IS A WAL DECISION — do not 'fix' it to player_state.updated_at (mutant M9 exists for that). Reliability measured hr_leaderboard_refresh doing 11,188 inserts + 11,175 deletes over 34h on a ~107-row board, all decoded by Realtime's walrus and discarded, on an instance starved enough to be dropping player save writes ~100x/hour. The instinct was to hand-roll upsert-and-prune; MEASURED, that would have been wrong work, because `refresh materialized view concurrently` ALREADY diffs — on the replay, 0 of 32 rows are rewritten when nothing changed, against 32 of 32 for a plain refresh. The churn came from ROW CONTENT: player_state.updated_at is stamped on every ~90s settle, so every active player's rows changed every refresh and the diff had nothing to save (measured: ALL players settling with no score change rewrote 32 of 32). The production arithmetic corroborates a working diff over volatile content rather than a full rebuild — 11,188/408 refreshes ≈ 27 rows each ≈ the active quarter of the board, where a non-diffing rebuild would have been 408 × 107 ≈ 43,656. The column also RENDERS NOTHING: src/features/leaderboards.js normRow() copies it to `savedAt` (:186) and nothing reads it again; the 'updated Nm ago' stamp comes from the board-level refreshed_at in leaderboard_meta. So the column is kept (as null, exactly as the clan_power branch always did) to preserve the read shape, and simply not sourced. Steady-state refresh WAL is now zero: measured idle 0 rewritten, all-players-settled 0 rewritten, and a real xp gain still rewrites — the paired positive, without which a matview that had stopped updating would satisfy every zero. §6(h2) refuses a non-null saved_at and LB-12 grades both directions. If a 'last active' signal is ever wanted, source it as date_trunc('day', …) so it churns once a day, and re-measure. ⚠⚠ REVERSIBILITY — RE-APPLYING 2026-08-08-leaderboards.sql IS NOT A SUPPORTED REVERT PATH; DO NOT RUN THAT FILE AGAINST A LIVE DATABASE (Security review C2). It is written for a 2026-08-08 database and does TWO destructive things, only one of which is visible in its own output: (1) `grant select on leaderboard_ranked to anon, authenticated` (:208) re-opens the F5 direct-matview dump of every player's uuid and display name; and (2) `create or replace function public.hr_leaderboard(...)` (:287) + `grant execute to anon, authenticated` (:357) OVERWRITES the A9 rate-gate wrapper installed by §4 of 2026-08-11-authenticated-surface-lockdown.sql, leaving an ungated anon-callable unrate-limited RPC — it never mentions the gate, so it reports success while removing it. The SUPPORTED revert is a new FORWARD migration: nothing here holds state (leaderboard_ranked is derived data), so copy the SELECT body out of the 2026-08-08 file's §3 and the reader body out of its §6 BY HAND, recreate the matview with `revoke all` (never that file's grant), replace hr_leaderboard__ungated (never the public name), and touch neither the A9 wrapper nor its grants. If someone runs the old file anyway, re-apply §4 of 2026-08-11-authenticated-surface-lockdown.sql (re-runnable — it skips already-wrapped targets via v_n_skip) AND 2026-08-14-leaderboard-view-lockdown.sql, in that order, then verify with §6(b)/§6(i) or LB-5/LB-11. Safe to re-run. Graded by tests/leaderboard-server-source.mjs.
_order_notes.2026-08-18-skill-row-upsert.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED. It TAKES OVER from 2026-08-18-equip-release-codes.sql as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_apply, and must therefore sit after it: applied the other way round, equip-release-codes would silently restore the bare UPDATE and the incident would come back with every self-check in both files still green. The body is GENERATED by tools/derive-skill-row-upsert.mjs from equip-release-codes and patched at ONE named anchor (the XP grant); `node tools/derive-skill-row-upsert.mjs --check` runs in the smoke suite, so it cannot be hand-edited. Its §0 REFUSES to install unless the LIVE body already carries b366's `too_many_equip_ops` (i.e. it IS equip-release-codes' body) and unless hr_skills is non-empty — the new true-unknown check would otherwise refuse every XP key and turn a bookkeeping gap into a total accrual outage. What it ships: hr_apply's XP grant stops being `update player_skills ...; if row_count <> 1 then hr_reject('unknown_skill')` and becomes a TRUE-UNKNOWN check against hr_skills followed by `insert ... on conflict (user_id, slot, skill_id) do update set xp = player_skills.xp + v_n`. Why: the old form conflated "that skill is not in the catalogue" with "this character has no row for a real skill", and per-skill rows are seeded ONCE at character creation (2026-08-14-character-bootstrap.sql) while the catalogue grows afterwards — so when Stonemason shipped, every pre-Stonemason character got `unknown_skill` on a legitimate grant, the refusal STORED itself against the intent key so "Try again" replayed it, and because hr_reject rolls the protected block back WHOLE each refusal also discarded the window's ore, gold and every other skill's XP. 51 aggregated rejections at severity `incident` in one night. ⚠ THE ORDER OF THE TWO STATEMENTS IS LOAD-BEARING and §3(b) asserts it: there is NO foreign key from player_skills.skill_id to hr_skills (the FK is to player_state(user_id, slot)), so an upsert that ran before the catalogue check would mint a skill row from a client string. ⚠ PRODUCTION WAS BACKFILLED BY HAND on the night of the incident (all user/slot × hr_skills pairs exist), so this file repairs no data and must be — and is — correct on a fresh database too. Behaviour-WIDENING only: every delta the previous body accepted is accepted with an identical result, `unknown_skill` is raised strictly more narrowly, and reverting is re-applying equip-release-codes. The character-bootstrap seed is untouched and already correct; §3(g) asserts it still seeds from hr_skills. Real predecessors: everything equip-release-codes names, plus 2026-08-11-catalogue.generated.sql for hr_skills (§0 refuses without rows) and 2026-08-14-character-bootstrap.sql (§3(g)). SAFE IN EITHER ORDER with the Edge deploy — no payload change accompanies it. Graded by tests/skill-row-upsert.mjs and PART 1f-ii of tests/run-sql-tests.mjs.
_order_notes.2026-08-18-clan-deposit-ownership.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (Security review REQUIRED — it MOVES AUTHORITY: item possession for the clan Storehouse). LAST OF ALL, though nothing forces it to be: it touches NO body any derivation chain grades — not hr_apply, not hr_rate_gate, not hr_perks_of, not hr_assert_grant_hygiene — and takes over no role from anyone. What it ships: public.clan_deposit__ungated(uuid,jsonb) gains the ownership debit ported from hr_market_list §(d) (read player_inventory `for update`, refuse `insufficient_item` when short, delete rather than store a zero row), and its write section moves inside a PROTECTED BLOCK so every refusal raises HR000 through hr_reject and rolls the WHOLE deposit back — the 2026-08-08 body returned ok:false from inside the item loop AFTER earlier iterations had already written clan_stores and clan_ledger, which with a debit in the same loop would commit a half-transfer. The character slot is DERIVED (prefer 0, else the lowest the caller owns) because the signature cannot grow a parameter: clan_deposit(uuid,jsonb) is A9-wrapped and pinned in tests/rpc-resolution.targets.json, so a third argument would be a new overload and PostgREST resolution would go ambiguous. ⚠ IT REPLACES THE __ungated TWIN, NOT THE PUBLIC NAME — replacing public.clan_deposit(uuid,jsonb) would swap the A9 wrapper for an ungated body and delete the rate gate (2026-08-11-authenticated-surface-lockdown.sql §6, 'The one-way door'); §0(a) REFUSES to install without the retrofit and §2(e) asserts the wrapper still references hr_rpc_gate afterwards. Real predecessors: 2026-08-08-clan-seat.sql (the body, hr_castle_items, hr_utc_day_key, hr_clan_decay_cp), 2026-08-11-authenticated-surface-lockdown.sql (the rename), 2026-08-11-player-state.sql (player_inventory + player_state), 2026-08-11-apply-engine.sql (hr_reject). §0 refuses on each, with a positive AND a negative body-scan control. Safe to re-run (§0(d) notices a re-apply rather than refusing). Reversibility: re-apply the §7 body from clan-seat under the __ungated name. Graded by tests/clan-deposit-ownership.mjs and by PART 1h of tests/run-sql-tests.mjs.
_order_notes.2026-08-18-equip-release-codes.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (Security review REQUIRED — Phase 2 of docs/design/live-settlement.md MOVES AUTHORITY). LAST OF ALL, and it TAKES OVER from 2026-08-17-fight-carry.sql as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_apply. The body is GENERATED by tools/derive-equip-release.mjs from fight-carry and patched at ONE named anchor (c_release_codes); `node tools/derive-equip-release.mjs --check` runs in the smoke suite, so it cannot be hand-edited. Applied BEFORE fight-carry it would be silently deleted by it — and its own §0 REFUSES that case, because it asserts the Phase 0 anchors are already in the LIVE body before it replaces anything. What it ships: five equip refusal codes (bad_equip, unknown_equip_slot, wrong_slot, requirement_not_met, too_many_equip_ops) join c_release_codes, so a catalogue-staleness refusal against a player equip cannot brick the intent key — the b361 `unknown_skill` incident applied BEFORE the equivalent incident rather than after it. insufficient_item is DELIBERATELY NOT released (it is the equip block's ownership check; releasing it hands a client unlimited free re-attempts on one key against a moving inventory) and §3(c) asserts that negative against the ARRAY LITERAL rather than against the body, because the body legitimately mentions the code elsewhere and a naive substring test would fail for the wrong reason. Real predecessors: everything fight-carry names, plus 2026-08-11-catalogue.generated.sql for hr_equip_slots/hr_item_slots, which §3(f) refuses to run without. SAFE IN EITHER ORDER with the Edge deploy: an old payload never reaches the equip block, and a new payload against an unpatched database gets correct refusals with a stickier key.
_order_notes.2026-08-17-fight-carry.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (Security review REQUIRED before it deploys — the design gate in docs/design/live-settlement.md §10 PHASE 0). LAST OF ALL, and it TAKES OVER from 2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_apply, AND from 2026-08-15-tool-carry.sql as the last that may replace hr_state_of. Both bodies are GENERATED by tools/derive-fight-carry.mjs from those two files and patched at named anchors (hr_apply five, hr_state_of one); `node tools/derive-fight-carry.mjs --check` runs in the smoke suite, so neither can be hand-edited. Applied BEFORE gem-daily-budget it would be silently deleted by it, taking the whole in-flight-fight carry with it while the column survived — the engine would keep proposing a `fight` key at an hr_apply that refuses unknown keys, and every combat window would 409. What it ships: player_state.fight (jsonb, ONE column not three — see the file header for why the self-configuring switch needs a non-null container), the `fight` delta key with an hp re-clamp against hr_activities.max_hp, and two independent void-on-activity-change rules. Real predecessors: player-state (the table), 2026-08-11-catalogue.generated.sql (hr_activities.max_hp, which its §0 REFUSES to install without — the clamp reads it and a missing ceiling would 409 every fight), apply-engine + intent-key-hygiene + tool-carry + gem-daily-budget (the hr_apply body), auto-eat + tool-carry (the hr_state_of body). ⚠⚠ STANDING RULE, SECURITY F5 (2026-08-16) — A MONSTER'S HP IS NOW A DEPLOY-ORDER DEPENDENCY. Any change to a monster's `hp` in src/data/monsters.js requires re-applying 2026-08-11-catalogue.generated.sql BEFORE the Edge payload deploys. PINNED SHIP ORDER, every time: (1) node tools/gen-catalogues.mjs, (2) apply 2026-08-11-catalogue.generated.sql, (3) apply 2026-08-17-fight-carry.sql (first time only), (4) deploy the Edge payload. Why: hr_activities.max_hp is the ceiling this file re-derives a carried fight.hp against, and the engine seeds/emits that hp from src/data/monsters.js. Raise a monster's HP payload-first and every honest checkpoint for it proposes an hp ABOVE the stale ceiling — refused `bad_fight_hp`, which is not on index.ts's DEGRADABLE list, so it 409s the whole window for every player fighting that monster. Lower it payload-first and the mirror happens quietly: the ceiling stays high and the clamp is simply wider than the game. The blast radius is bounded to one window per player rather than to a day because `bad_fight*` is in c_release_codes and releases the intent key (Security F3) — but a bounded outage is still an outage, and the fix is this ordering, not that release. Graded by tests/live-settlement.mjs and PART 1f-ii of tests/run-sql-tests.mjs.
_order_notes.2026-08-16-day-budget-artisan.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). It TAKES OVER from 2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql as the last file that may `create or replace` hr_day_budget_limits, and must therefore sit after it: applied the other way round, gem-daily-budget's §2 would silently restore the pre-artisan ceilings (qty 1,000,000 / xp 40,000,000) and the qty fuse would fire on the twenty-fifth minute of an ordinary fletching night, with every self-check in both files still green — the clan_members "join as self" defect applied to a constant. Its §0 REFUSES to install unless the live body already carries c_day_gems_budget (i.e. it IS the b351 four-dimension body it was derived from) and unless the live ceilings are either the values it was measured against or the values it installs, with a positive and a negative scan control so a blind prosrc scan cannot report a clean bill. It also refuses against an hr_apply whose per-call clamps have drifted, because the whole argument for raising the DAY ceilings is that the PER-CALL ones are held: Security ruling 2026-08-16 HOLDS c_max_xp_delta at 12000000 (it cannot rise — xpForLevel(99) is 13034431) and c_max_item_delta at 1000000 (the ammunition lane trips it and is paid through the degrade ladder pending a YIELD ruling). It touches NO other body: not hr_apply (2026-08-15-gem-daily-budget.sql remains the last file that may replace it), not hr_day_budget_used, not hr_day_budget_check, and it adds no object, no table and no grant that did not already exist. Why it exists: b356 made `artisan` payable — 290 of the 344 hr_activities rows — and 2026-08-11-daily-budget.sql sized the ceilings against combat alone, saying so in its own header (the headroom was left "for the gathering, artisan and farm accrual slices that do not exist yet"). Reversibility is re-applying gem-daily-budget. Real predecessors: daily-budget (the three primitives), gem-daily-budget (the four-dimension body it restates), apply-engine (the per-call clamps its §0 and §3 assert are unmoved). Graded by tests/accrual-engine.mjs' dayBudgetGuard, which reads the ceilings out of the LAST migration in the chain that declares them.
_order_notes.2026-08-17-cutover-import.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies it during the freeze). LAST in the chain because it reads six catalogues (hr_items / hr_skills / hr_equip_slots / hr_item_slots / hr_crops / hr_unlocks) and calls three functions (hr_create_character, hr_state_of, hr_level_from_xp), and its §0 refuses to install without any of them — in particular without the player_progress_unlock_guard trigger that 2026-08-16-artisan-progress-model.sql installs, because the import is the first bulk writer of kind='unlock' rows this database has ever had. Graded by tests/cutover-import.mjs.
_order_notes.2026-08-10-dr-beta-invites-base.sql: Reconstruction of a production object with no migration file. Must precede authenticated-surface-lockdown (A9's retrofit list names claim_beta_invite(text) and fails closed on it) and live-market-rls (§3 reads public.beta_invites).
_order_notes.2026-08-10-dr-bug-reports-base.sql: Reconstruction of a production object with no migration file. Must precede bug-report-relay, which ALTERs the table and creates bug_report_submit — which A9 then retrofits.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-player-state.sql: The foundation. Nine 2026-08-11 files depend on it and five of them sort before it alphabetically.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-clan-membership-authority.sql: Before clan-write-policy-pin and raid-claim-authority: all three once defined clan_members "join as self"; this file now owns the definition and the other two assert against whatever is live. Applying them the other way round silently deletes R4's timestamp pin — see HANDOFF, 'A LATENT BUG WORTH MORE THAN THE FEATURE THAT FOUND IT'.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-authenticated-surface-lockdow: The A9 __ungated retrofit. Every later file that references a *__ungated name depends on it, and it in turn needs every RPC it retrofits to already exist — so it sits after the whole clan/raid/market surface and before the 08-13 files.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-daily-budget.sql: Before apply-engine: apply-engine §0 fails CLOSED without hr_day_budget_check. Applying them the other way round is a refused migration, not a slow degradation.
_order_notes.2026-08-11-grant-hygiene.sql: Last of the 08-11 block: it is the detector, so it must see the finished surface. It reports every un-retrofitted RPC, which makes it a second, independent check that A9 ran.
_order_notes.2026-08-15-auto-eat.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED to production yet — in 'order' rather than 'excluded' for the same reason 2026-08-14-character-bootstrap.sql is: the replay is how a staged migration gets EXECUTED before anyone applies it, and its self-verifying block is the commit gate. It REPLACES hr_state_of, so it must sit after apply-engine; it reads hr_items.auto_eatable, so the catalogue must be regenerated (it is, in this repo) and RE-APPLIED to production before this file. APPLIED to production 2026-08-15, together with the regenerated catalogue.
_order_notes.2026-08-15-activity-intent.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies), but it belongs in 'order' rather than 'excluded' because a rebuilt database SHOULD have it — same treatment as 2026-08-14-leaderboard-view-lockdown.sql. Last, and it has four real predecessors: accrue-gate (it replaces hr_rate_gate), catalogue (hr_activities), apply-engine (§0 refuses to install against an hr_apply with no intent_mismatch branch or no S5 accrued_to stamp) and character-bootstrap (§4 drives a real character).
_order_notes.2026-08-15-intent-key-hygiene.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). LAST, and it must stay last of anything that touches hr_apply: it is a `create or replace` of the WHOLE hr_apply body, derived programmatically from 2026-08-11-apply-engine.sql (byte-identical to production, md5 917967d4bb03ca1c098b3e896a3e8317, compared 2026-08-15) and patched at four anchors. _order_notes.2026-08-17-bug-triage.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED (the Coordinator applies). Adds the operator half of the bug-report pipe to public.bug_reports: status ('new'|'triaged'|'fixed'|'wontfix', the new authority), triage_note, triaged_at, a partial index on the BACKLOG so the queue read does not scale with the archive, and two BEFORE triggers. bug_reports_triage_sync_trg DERIVES the pre-existing `resolved` bit from status and stamps triaged_at from the server clock, so the legacy boolean can never disagree with the status and no caller can backdate a triage. bug_reports_insert_guard_trg is a per-user 40/day BACKSTOP — deliberately double bug_report_submit's own 20/day so it never fires on legitimate traffic — closing the one unrated write path: the direct-PostgREST fallback insert admitted by the 'bugs anyone submits' policy, which never crosses the RPC that holds the 6/hour + 20/day cap. hr_rate_gate could not be reused (granted solely to hr_engine, keyed (user,slot,bucket) for the accrual engine, unreachable from a client insert). It touches NO function body — not hr_apply, not hr_rate_gate, not hr_assert_grant_hygiene — so it is outside all three derivation chains and takes over no role from anyone. Its §4(f) asserts bug_report_submit is still a SINGLE function: the file deliberately adds no RPC parameter, because `create or replace` keys on arity, so a 7-arg version would be a NEW OVERLOAD beside the 6-arg one pinned in tests/rpc-resolution.targets.json and mirrored by the A9 `bug_report_submit__ungated` twin — PostgREST resolution would go ambiguous and the ungated census would grow an unretrofitted entry. Screenshots are deliberately NOT stored (they are already Discord attachments; a base64 copy would inflate the only database holding player progression, and restores here run off daily backups). Must follow 2026-08-10-dr-bug-reports-base.sql (the table) and 2026-08-11-bug-report-relay.sql (the INSERT policy and the RPC arity its §0 and §4 assert). Safe to re-run; the status backfill is guarded so it cannot walk back an operator's decision. Graded by tests/bug-triage.mjs.

excluded.2026-08-12-clan-members-rls-drop.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED, and it REFUSES to apply by design: its precondition needs a real clan_ledger row of kind='member', i.e. a player who joined through clan_join(). A fresh rebuild has no such row, so the file correctly raises. That refusal is the file working, not the chain failing.
